A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same off-policy adversarial imitation learning study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MiniGrid and MuJoCo experiments in Section 5 and Figures 1–2, with implementation details in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original MiniGrid results using policy-gradient updates in Appendix D and Figure 3.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 generalizes the replay-window specification from fixed N to round-dependent N(k). Appendix D additionally explores policy-gradient updates on MiniGrid. The core mirror-descent policy update and projected reward-ascent objectives remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate EmptyRoom grids of sizes 3×3, 5×5, and 9×9, plus HalfCheetah-v2, Hopper-v2, and Walker2d-v2. The new policy-gradient experiment uses the existing MiniGrid tasks without adding environments or task requirements.

E2.justification: Figures 1–2 retain their comparison groups. Figure 3 repeats the MiniGrid comparison of N=1, 4, 32, and 128 with an expert reference, using policy-gradient updates throughout. Newly cited alternative learning methods are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds a MiniGrid evaluation condition using policy-gradient updates instead of Figure 1's model-based updates. The original experiments' training budgets, evaluation metrics, demonstration counts, and settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 3 tests whether replay benefits persist when MiniGrid policy updates use policy gradients. This adds a focused robustness check across the three retained room sizes; the original replay-depth analyses remain.

E5.justification: MiniGrid results retain five seeds with standard-deviation shading, and MuJoCo results retain ten seeds with standard-error shading. Figure 3 follows the existing MiniGrid reporting convention rather than introducing a new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: The plotted results in Figures 1–2 are identical. Figure 3 adds policy-gradient learning curves showing benefits from replay; N=32 outperforms N=128 in EmptyRoom-5×5, while their performance is nearly equal in EmptyRoom-9×9. These are additional results under a different updater, not improvements to the original runs.

T1.justification: Theorems 4.4 and B.8 expand the stated reward-regret guarantees from fixed N to schedules N(k), with revised error terms and appendix derivations; Proposition 4.7 is generalized accordingly. Theorems 4.4–4.5 correct eta from 1/sqrt(K) to sqrt(SA/K), matching v1's Appendix A.3 proof. The standalone combined linear-MDP Theorem B.9 is removed, although its component bounds remain.

C1.justification: v2 removes the claim of providing the first theoretical guarantees for off-policy AIL from the abstract, first contribution, and conclusion. The substantive convergence, sample-efficiency, and empirical-performance claims are retained.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 adds discussion of why alternative policy optimizers must satisfy stability as well as low regret. Appendix D interprets the new policy-gradient results as supporting replay benefits beyond model-based updates and a larger useful replay window as state space grows. Existing neural-network and N=K qualifications remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C removes both implementation pointers: the MiniGrid repository link and the statement linking to Shani et al.'s code for MuJoCo. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, and runtime details remain. The new policy-gradient experiment lacks a dedicated implementation description.

R1.justification: v2 adds context on behavioral cloning, offline RL, and occupancy matching, positioning its contribution as theoretical support for AIL rather than a competing imitation-learning framework. It also discusses FTRL, FPL, and policy-gradient alternatives with new citations. The existing AIL literature discussion remains largely intact.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. Changes include additional positioning and policy-update explanations, updated affiliations, author-year citations, removal of acknowledgments, and replacement of the generic Broad Impact appendix with Additional Experimental Results.

P2.justification: The journal template changes typography, text width, running headers, author-block arrangement, spacing, and figure sizing and placement throughout. Figures 1–2 retain their plotted content, while a new three-panel Figure 3 is added.

improvement.justification: The step-size correction resolves a mismatch between the theorem statements and their existing proof, while Figure 3 adds a useful check of replay benefits under another policy updater. These modest gains in coherence and empirical support are offset partly by removal of both implementation links and sparse documentation of the new experiment.
